text:
**Yes, but only some models, and it isn't automatic.** A power station only works as a UPS if it documents UPS/EPS behavior with automatic switchover. Anker says a basic power station can keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS during an outage ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).

**What to check**
- **Transfer time:** Look for a published switchover of about 10 ms or less. EcoFlow warns that 20-30 ms or more can cause data loss ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). That is a manufacturer's claim. Anker is more measured: 10-20 ms suits some devices, but it isn't 0 ms, so check your computer's or PSU's manual ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- **Pure sine wave output** and support for continuous pass-through use.
- **Enough wattage:** Total your computer's running draw, ideally measured with a plug-in watt meter, and compare it to the continuous output rating.
- **Runtime:** Hours ≈ Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. For example, 1,000 Wh at 100 W gives about 8.5 hours at best.
- **When to skip it:** If the device needs 0 ms transfer, continuous voltage regulation, or standard UPS communication, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice. The Anker NAS article above makes the same point.

**Models with a published UPS switchover time**
- **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2):** 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W, UPS switchover ≤15 ms. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF according to the retailer page ([listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). That's an affiliate link, and checkout has the final word on price. At up to 15 ms it's the slowest of these, so confirm your computer tolerates it.
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups):** 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, listed at $699.99 after coupon. This link goes to Anker's article, since I didn't have a product page.
- **[EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply):** 600 W output, switchover under 10 ms, and plenty for a desktop plus drives. This link goes to EcoFlow's article, not a store page.

EcoFlow's DELTA 3 pages have a UPS FAQ, but the snippets don't include the switching time. Check it on the [DELTA 3 Classic support page](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-classic-portable-power-station/support) before buying.

For a typical desktop, a UPS-rated station with 10 ms or less switchover is a reasonable choice if you want hours of runtime. If you only need a few minutes to shut down safely, or your gear demands 0 ms, a regular or online UPS is the better fit.
